$comment: The deployment profile: everything a person or the model READS that is specific to what this deployment is for. These defaults are the base product in NEUTRAL words: an account, a member, its account owner, a delivery, a project and its plan. Base text never spells a role or a record word; it writes a placeholder ({account}, {deployment}, {implementation}, {rollout}, {member}, {owner}) filled from here, and a deployment's own profile supplies its domain's words. A deployment changes them by ADDING profiles/NN-<name>.json files (later files win, objects merge deeply, arrays replace); nothing here is edited. Identifiers never change with a profile: database columns, API routes, tool names and data-room path tokens stay as they are. The data-room folder names are the profile's too (dataroom.domains.<id>.folder): neutral here, and pinned by a deployment that already stores files under other names. See docs/DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE.md.

dataroom.$comment: Each data-room domain has an id (the key below: what code and other profiles call it), a `folder` (the name its files are STORED under, the first segment of every path in it) and a `label` (what people and the model read; when a profile gives none it is the folder's name). The folder is a setting of the deployment, not of the code: a deployment that already holds files states the folder names it has, and they are never moved. `uploads_folder` is where files a person attaches are stored. See docs/DEPLOYMENT_PROFILE.md, "Stored folder names".

domains.$comment: The two record areas a deployment may REDEFINE rather than hide: what each is called, what its fields and enum values are shown as, which fields are not used (hidden; a hidden required field carries a fixed value the forms submit). Field keys are the real ones (agent/lib/customer-schema.ts, agent/lib/db/schema.ts) and option keys are real enum values; both are checked at build. custom_fields are the deployment's OWN fields on an area (key, label, type, required, options, help, show_in_list), stored by key in the table's `custom` column; the default declares none. These defaults are today's labels.

persona.$comment: base: the root agent's built-in persona (the operations orchestrator, its specialist roster, the system-of-record and stand-up sections). false drops it: the root prompt keeps only its neutral rules, and a pack's agent/instructions/50-pack-*.md supplies who the agent is.

specialists.$comment: exclude: base specialists (directory names under agent/subagents/) this deployment does not use. Nothing is moved: their directories stay; they are left out of the subagent registry, every prompt's roster and list of names, the provisioned workflow library, and the eve build (scripts/eve-build.mjs hides them from eve only while it builds).

account_fields.$comment: hidden: fields of the account record itself (the customer row: arr, seats, aeOwner, renewalDate, platform, tickets, …) this deployment does not use. They are removed from what the MODEL reads and writes: the record tools' parameters and every record they return. Storage, the API, the CLI and the forms are unchanged, and a value already stored is kept when the model writes the record. Keys are customerSchema keys in agent/lib/customer-schema.ts; id and name cannot be hidden. The two redefinable areas hide their own fields under domains.<area>.fields.<key>.hidden. custom_fields: the deployment's OWN fields on the account record (a company's notes, a site's permit number), with the same spec as domains.<area>.custom_fields (key, label, type, required, options, help, show_in_list). Their values live by key in the customers table's custom jsonb column and every write is validated by agent/lib/custom-fields.ts. None by default.
